skills.name: agent-prompt
skills.title: Prompt for an agent
skills.description: Goal, context, constraints, done when. Turns a spoken request into instructions for a coding or chat agent; use in an AI assistant app.

examples.input: okay so I want you to add a dark mode toggle to the settings page of my react app um the settings are in src slash settings dot tsx we use tailwind don't add any new dependencies and keep the existing theme context and it's done when the toggle persists after a reload I think the theme context is in src slash theme but I'm not sure
examples.output:
Goal: Add a dark mode toggle to the settings page of my React app.
Context:
- The settings page is in src/settings.tsx.
- The app uses Tailwind.
- I think the theme context is in src/theme, but I'm not sure.
Constraints:
- Don't add any new dependencies.
- Keep the existing theme context.
Done when:
- The toggle persists after a reload.

skills.name: clean-podcast

examples.input:
**Jo:** so welcome back um today I've got Priya Shah who runs the community garden on Elm Street. Priya how did it start

**Priya:** it started in 2019 with like six of us and a skip full of pallets and we, we, we honestly had no idea what we were doing

**Jo:** we'll hear how it grew right after this.

**Jo:** this episode is supported by Greenleaf Seeds. go to greenleaf dot com slash garden and use code JO for 15 percent off your first order.

**Jo:** okay back to it. so how many members have you got now

**Priya:** about 80, and we track the plots in a shared Google Sheet which, you know, is all you need really
examples.output:
**Jo:** So welcome back. Today I've got Priya Shah, who runs the community garden on Elm Street. Priya, how did it start?

**Priya:** It started in 2019 with 6 of us and a skip full of pallets, and we honestly had no idea what we were doing.

skills.name: flashcards
skills.title: Flashcards
skills.description: Question and answer cards to revise from. Turns a lecture, talk, podcast or voice note into flashcards, one fact each; use after a class or anything you want to remember.

examples.input: **Dr Okafor:** okay so today is osmosis. osmosis is the movement of water across a partially permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one. sorry about the projector by the way, facilities are coming at 3. so why does it matter, well a plant cell in pure water swells and becomes turgid, which is what keeps the stem upright. in salty water it loses water and we call that plasmolysis. three things speed osmosis up, a steeper concentration gradient, a higher temperature, and a larger surface area.
examples.output:
**Q:** What is osmosis?

**A:** The movement of water across a partially permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one.

**Q:** What happens to a plant cell in pure water?

**A:** It swells and becomes turgid.

**Q:** What keeps a plant's stem upright?

**A:** Its cells being turgid.

**Q:** What is plasmolysis?

**A:** A plant cell losing water in salty water.

**Q:** How does the concentration gradient affect the rate of osmosis?

**A:** A steeper gradient speeds osmosis up.

**Q:** How does temperature affect the rate of osmosis?

**A:** A higher temperature speeds osmosis up.

**Q:** How does surface area affect the rate of osmosis?

**A:** A larger surface area speeds osmosis up.

skills.name: flowchart

examples.input: so when a return comes in first we check the receipt if there's no receipt we offer store credit only if there is a receipt we check whether it's within thirty days if it is we refund to the card otherwise it's store credit too and then either way we log it in the returns sheet
examples.output:
flowchart TD
    n1{"Has a receipt?"}
    n1 -->|"No"| n2["Offer store credit only"]
    n1 -->|"Yes"| n3{"Within 30 days?"}
    n3 -->|"Yes"| n4["Refund to the card"]
    n3 -->|"No"| n2
    n2 --> n5(["Log it in the returns sheet"])
    n4 --> n5

skills.name: lecture-notes
skills.title: Lecture notes
skills.description: Study notes by topic, with questions from the room kept apart. Turns a recorded lecture, class or talk into notes; use after a lecture or training session.

examples.input:
**Dr Lee:** Today, supply and demand. The equilibrium price is where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded. If the government sets a ceiling below it, you get a shortage. Second topic, elasticity. Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity over the percentage change in price.

**Speaker 2:** Does the shortage thing apply to rent control?

**Dr Lee:** Yes, the same shortage appears.
examples.output:
### Supply and demand
- **Equilibrium price** is where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded
- A government ceiling below the equilibrium price causes a shortage
### Elasticity
- **Price elasticity of demand** is the percentage change in quantity over the percentage change in price
### Questions from the room
- Does the shortage apply to rent control? Yes, the same shortage appears

skills.name: meeting-notes
skills.title: Conversation notes
skills.description: Decisions, actions and what each person raised. Turns a meeting, call or 1:1 into notes, with presets for the sections to keep; use after a meeting, call or check-in.

examples.input: okay Sam here quick recap of the venue meeting for the conference um we agreed on the Riverside Hall over the hotel because it's cheaper and has the bigger stage Tom's going to send the deposit by next Tuesday I'll call the caterer about vegetarian options and we decided to cap tickets at 250 we still don't know if we're doing a livestream and someone needs to ask about parking but nobody grabbed that one
examples.output:
### Summary
The group chose the Riverside Hall for the conference and capped tickets at 250. Whether to livestream is still open.
### Decisions
- Use the Riverside Hall over the hotel
- Cap tickets at 250
### Actions
#### Tom
- [ ] Send the deposit by next Tuesday

#### Sam
- [ ] Call the caterer about vegetarian options

#### Unassigned
- [ ] Ask about parking
### Open questions
- Whether to do a livestream

skills.name: takeaways
skills.title: Key takeaways
skills.description: The claims and advice worth keeping, each with its reason. Turns a podcast, talk, lecture or voice note into its key takeaways, most important first; use when you want the point of a recording without rereading it.

examples.input: so the big thing from the trial is that the four day week didn't cut output, revenue was actually up 1.4 percent across the 61 companies. um if you like the show please rate and subscribe. the second thing is sick days fell by about two thirds, 65 percent. and honestly the companies that struggled were the ones that just squeezed five days into four without cutting any meetings, so you have to cut meetings first. 56 of the 61 kept it going after the trial ended.
examples.output:
- **The four-day week didn't cut output.** Revenue was up 1.4 percent across the 61 companies in the trial.
- **Sick days fell by about two thirds.** They dropped 65 percent.
- **Cut meetings before moving to four days.** The companies that struggled squeezed 5 days into 4 without cutting any meetings.
- **Most companies kept the four-day week.** 56 of the 61 kept it going after the trial ended.
